text:
My dashboard said average latency was 50ms. Customers were still complaining.

Turns out a few slow requests were hiding in the average. p99 was 4 seconds. Most users were fine; the unlucky ones were furious — and they were the ones writing support tickets.

Two metrics people mix up:

• Latency — how long one request takes
• Throughput — how many requests you handle per second

You can have great throughput and terrible tail latency. Or low average latency with a long tail that ruins checkout.

Percentiles (p95, p99) beat averages for anything user-facing. SLAs should name the percentile, not "we're fast on average."

I wrote up how I read latency vs throughput, why tails matter, and how teams actually define SLAs.
